title: CMC Readiness Issues at FDA End-of-Phase 2 and Pre-NDA/Pre-BLA Meetings
summary: The CMC gaps FDA raises at End-of-Phase 2 and pre-NDA/pre-BLA meetings, and how they changed submission timing, content and review outcomes.
body_markdown:
## CMC readiness at FDA End-of-Phase 2 and pre-NDA/pre-BLA meetings: recurring issues and their effect on submission timing and content


Chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) readiness is one of the most frequent sources of friction in FDA milestone meetings. Meeting minutes and review documents in Drugs@FDA and CBER approval packages show a consistent pattern. At End-of-Phase 2 (EOP2), FDA focuses on regulatory starting materials, specifications, dissolution methods, and whether the Phase 3 formulation will be the commercial one. At pre-NDA and pre-BLA meetings, the discussion shifts to whether the application will be complete on day one: enough stability data, process validation, comparability data, extractables and leachables (E&L) data, impurity qualification, and inspection-ready facilities.


The consequences show up in four ways: data FDA requires in the original application, negotiated "late component" windows (typically 30 days), warnings of refusal to file, and, where advice was not followed, major amendments or Complete Response Letters (CRLs).


### Key takeaways


- **Stability data is the main timing lever.** For NDAs, FDA's baseline is generally 12 months of long-term data on three primary batches at submission; biologics minutes often reference shorter packages (about 6 months). It has accepted 9 months, or 3 to 6 months, with a 30-day update in specific cases. Later updates risk being treated as a major amendment or not reviewed in the cycle[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=227)[231](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=231)[518](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=518)[527](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=527)[533](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=533) .
- **Process validation is not a "late component" for biologics.** FDA told the Opdivo sponsor that PPQ data could not follow the initial BLA by 45 days[453](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=453) . FDA told the Keytruda sponsor it could not accept an incomplete CMC package, and offered a choice between a complete December 2013 BLA and a rolling submission ending with PPQ data[449](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=449) .
- **Impurity and E&L gaps draw refuse-to-file warnings.** These warnings appear repeatedly in pre-NDA minutes[136](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=136)[139](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=139)[141](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=141)[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=143)[376](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=376)[393](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=393) . Where E&L advice was not followed, the result was a CRL or a resubmission requirement[385](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=385)[387](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=387)[420](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=420) .
- **Thin CMC briefing packages lead to extra meetings.** FDA has recommended separate CMC-only pre-NDA or CMC-specific EOP2 meetings when the package lacked usable CMC content[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=191)[225](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=225) .


### What FDA guidance says each meeting should cover


FDA's guidance *IND Meetings for Human Drugs and Biologics: Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Information* is the anchor document[408](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=408) . For EOP2, it identifies topics including product and cell bank characterization, bioassay suitability, removal of product- and process-related impurities, and the bioactivity of product-related substances and impurities. For conventional biologics, it adds facility-design coordination, process-validation considerations, and the potency assay[409](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=409) . The EOP2 background package should update the description of materials used or planned for Phase 3 and place completed studies in the context of the prospective NDA strategy[411](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=411) .


The same guidance places the pre-NDA/pre-BLA meeting about six months before submission. It frames the meeting around filing and review obstacles. The sponsor should assure FDA that the application will contain adequate stability data under protocols agreed at EOP2, and that all manufacturing, testing, and packaging facilities will be ready for inspection by the time of submission[337](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=337)[338](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=338)[339](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=339) .


For expedited programs, the guidance *Expedited Programs for Serious Conditions: Drugs and Biologics* recommends that sponsors seeking rolling review obtain preliminary agreement at or before the pre-NDA/pre-BLA meeting on the schedule and on which portions will arrive separately. FDA generally accepts only a complete, review-ready section, such as the entire CMC section. At its discretion, it may accept a reviewable subsection that is missing items such as final consistency-lot or long-term stability data[340](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=340)[341](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=341) . The guidance also lets FDA decide case by case how much manufacturing information is needed at submission versus approval. Sponsors should raise their CMC plan no later than the pre-NDA/pre-BLA meeting[342](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=342) .


For cell and gene therapies, FDA guidance asks sponsors to:


- make commercial-scale changes and demonstrate comparability before trials intended to support effectiveness[482](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=482) ;
- qualify a potency assay before those trials and validate it before licensure or BLA submission[484](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=484)[485](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=485) ;
- justify the number of PPQ batches rather than relying on a fixed minimum[469](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=469) .


The draft comparability guidance warns that extensive changes shortly before BLA submission call for comprehensive comparability evidence and may require additional PPQ[467](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=467) .


### End-of-Phase 2: starting materials, specifications, and the to-be-marketed product


#### Regulatory starting materials and drug substance specifications


EOP2 CMC minutes most often record FDA conditionally accepting starting materials while deferring final judgment to NDA review. Two examples show the range:


- **Xtandi (NDA 203415):** FDA could not assess the proposed starting materials from the information supplied. It asked for reference standards, starting-material assays, impurity information, and supplier audit and change-control details. Drug substance specifications and genotoxic impurity controls were deferred to NDA review[181](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=181)[182](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=182) .
- **Gemtesa (NDA 213006):** FDA agreed to the starting-material designations on condition that the synthetic schemes appeared in the NDA. Final acceptance criteria and impurity controls were left for review, and FDA noted that the impurity-limit justification and a comprehensive potential-impurity list were missing[192](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=192)[193](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=193) .


Similar conditional outcomes appear for Cerdelga[185](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=185)[186](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=186) , Vistogard (where FDA offered a DMF route for the CMC information)[188](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=188)[189](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=189) , and the AbbVie Viekira Pak program, where FDA required specification justifications that weigh impurity rejection against manufacturing capability[194](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=194)[195](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=195) .


The practical effect is mostly on content. These issues rarely shift the timeline, but they predetermine what Module 3 must justify.


#### Dissolution methods


FDA used EOP2 to push back on non-discriminating or unjustified test methods. In the Xtandi program, FDA did not agree to replace capsule dissolution with a rupture test without justification. It recommended a test able to distinguish batches that are within specification from those that are not[181](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=181) . For Allegra-D 24 Hour, FDA wanted a discriminating method agreed as soon as possible, preferably before stability studies began[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=53)[54](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=54) .


The timing risk is concrete. In the Lipofen program, FDA said a bridging study would be needed if it disagreed with the dissolution conditions already used in NDA stability studies[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=223) . FDA reserved acceptability of the method and acceptance criteria for NDA review in many pre-NDA exchanges, including Khedezla, Hysingla ER, and a sertraline NDA[50](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=50)[51](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=51)[46](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=46) . In the sertraline case, FDA told the sponsor it could get earlier method feedback by amending the IND with a complete report, which typically took up to three months to assess[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=47)[48](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=48) .


#### Formulation bridging


Formulation decisions made at EOP2 can affect the whole clinical package:


- **Ojjaara (NDA 216873):** FDA expected the new tablet to meet 80 to 125% bioequivalence against the earlier capsule and wanted comparative PK results before the tablet was used in Phase 3. If the formulations were not bioequivalent, dose-finding and other completed studies would need to be repeated with tablets[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=32)[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=33) .
- **Jornay PM (NDA 209311):** FDA rejected an in vitro bridge between formulations that differed in manufacturing site and process. Given the product's complex release mechanism, it recommended a relative bioavailability study instead[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=28) .
- **Ibrance (NDA 207103):** At the pre-NDA stage, FDA said it preferred the pivotal-trial formulation to match the commercial product. It said in vivo bioequivalence offered the best assurance for major formulation changes[34](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=34)[35](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=35) .


#### Incomplete EOP2 CMC packages


When the EOP2 package lacked usable CMC content, FDA asked for another meeting. For Monoferric (NDA 208171), FDA could not find CMC information referenced in the package. It said it was unclear whether the available CMC information would support an NDA, and it recommended a separate CMC-specific EOP2 meeting[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=191) .


### Pre-NDA and pre-BLA: completeness of the application


#### Stability data at submission


Stability is the CMC topic most directly tied to submission timing. FDA described fewer than 12 months of long-term data in an original NDA as normally a filing issue[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=227) . Many minutes nonetheless record negotiated exceptions, usually with tight conditions.


Product FDA position at pre-NDA/pre-BLA stage Effect on timing or content


Zelboraf (NDA 202429) Accepted fewer than 12 months as an exception for early Module 3 submission, if the package represented the commercial product and process Updates limited to the same batches, process, and container closure. Any other CMC information could extend the review clock[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=227)[228](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=228)


Vabomere (NDA 209776) Agreed to the initial stability amounts plus updates Updates had to arrive within 4 months of submission. A later update would be a major amendment that could delay action[231](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=231)[232](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=232)


Uceris (NDA 205613) Initially refused less than 12 months long-term and 6 months accelerated data on 3 batches Agreed to 9 months at filing plus 12-month data within 30 days[518](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=518)


Zerbaxa (NDA 206829) Baseline of 12 months on 3 primary batches 9 months accepted if the update came within 30 days (no later than 60 days for priority review, or by mid-cycle for standard review)[527](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=527)


Trulance (NDA 208745) Permitted 3-month data as a late component Submitted within 30 days of the original NDA[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=236)


Amondys 45 (NDA 213026) Rejected the proposed mixed-duration package Recommended 12 months long-term plus 6 months accelerated per batch per strength. Warned of possible refusal to file[531](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=531)


Dartisla ODT (NDA 215019) Rejected the filing package Required 3 registration batches with 12 months long-term and 6 months accelerated data at submission. Did not pre-agree to an extrapolated 24-month expiry[535](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=535)


Austedo XR (NDA 216354) Would accept 9 months for review Would not commit to review an update arriving more than 30 days after submission[533](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=533)


Toviaz (NDA 022030) Would review added data if submitted at least 3 months before the goal date Data supported 18, not the requested 24, months of shelf life[521](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=521)


Keytruda (BLA 125514) Lack of commercial-scale stability data was a major concern. A complete package generally meant at least 6 months of stability data Offered a complete BLA or a rolling submission ending with initial PPQ data[449](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=449)[450](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=450)


Opdivo (BLA 125527) Generally expected 6 months of stability data from the Syracuse site in the initial BLA for the proposed shelf life Approval of the site also required drug product comparability data[454](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=454)[455](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=455)


Carvykti (BLA 125746) Pre-BLA agreement on a 30-day stability update The update and original data did not support the proposed shelf life. Later amendments did[267](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=267)


Two cross-cutting points emerge. First, a pre-meeting agreement on filing adequacy does not settle expiry dating. FDA repeatedly reserved shelf-life decisions for review[520](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=520)[522](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=522)[523](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=523)[533](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=533) . Second, filing with limited data is at the sponsor's risk. FDA told the paricalcitol sponsor that later data might not be reviewed and could yield a short expiry[532](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=532) , and gave a similar warning in the Qsymia program[537](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=537) . FDA also refused a supplier-qualification late component for the Zynrelef Kit that would have allowed an earlier filing, and required all qualification data at submission[536](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=536) .


#### Process validation and PPQ (biologics)


Pre-BLA minutes show that FDA treats process validation as part of a complete CMC package:


- **Opdivo:** FDA said process validation was not a limited component suitable for later submission under the PDUFA V approach, and rejected a 45-day post-submission timeline for PPQ data[453](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=453) .
- **Kymriah (BLA 125646):** At mid-cycle, FDA found that the process-validation lots were made before the protocol was approved and before the commercial process was established, using clinical batch records. FDA called this inconsistent with its pre-BLA recommendation. These were major CMC issues requiring resolution for approval[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=265)[266](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=266) .
- **Blincyto (BLA 125557):** FDA required BLA data showing that pilot-scale filling and lyophilization models represented the commercial processes[447](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=447) .
- **Ilaris (BLA 125319):** FDA listed the aseptic-processing validation, container closure integrity, sterilization, hold-time, media-fill, and lyophilization data it expected. It called the pre-meeting CMC package too general to judge completeness[425](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=425) .


#### Comparability after manufacturing changes


Late process, site, or equipment changes drew specific data requests:


- **Blincyto:** For comparability between process 4 and process 5 material, FDA asked for biological activity assay designs and all raw assay data, not only means[447](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=447)[448](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=448) .
- **Daxxify (BLA 761127):** FDA rejected the planned BLA content for an equipment upgrade. It required pre- and post-change comparability data, an E&L risk assessment, media-fill and sterilization validation, and capping validation[464](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=464) .
- **Adcetris:** For a manufacturing suite move, FDA said additional comparability studies were not needed if the equipment was the same or equivalent. All comparability data still belonged in the BLA, and facility changes would be evaluated at inspection[460](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=460)[461](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=461) .
- **Portrazza (BLA 125547):** Whether a manufacturing site needed full data in the original BLA depended on whether the sponsor sought that site's approval at licensure or in a supplement[458](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=458)[459](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=459) .
- **Breyanzi (BLA 125714):** At the pre-BLA meeting, FDA discussed specification acceptance criteria, potency, viability, shelf life, and a rolling submission. Module 3 arrived as the final rolling component. A later major amendment for substantial new manufacturing and facility information moved the PDUFA goal date to November 16, 2020. The record does not tie the amendment to a specific meeting issue[83](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=83)[84](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=84)[85](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=85) .


#### Potency assays


Potency assay readiness can change what goes into the BLA itself. For Prehevbrio (BLA 125737), the sponsor could not provide all the potency assay information requested at pre-BLA meetings. FDA considered the in vitro assay insufficiently developed and validated, and advised removing it from the BLA, release specifications, and stability plans. Further development was to continue under the IND or in a post-licensure prior-approval supplement[268](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=268) .


For Portrazza, FDA required a more robust package to justify dropping a binding potency assay from release and stability specifications[458](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=458) . For Repatha (BLA 125522), FDA would not yet accept substantially reduced stability testing of drug substance validation lots, and warned that missing data could prevent shelf-life support[456](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=456) .


#### Impurities, mutagenic impurities, and qualification


FDA's pre-NDA impurity advice is consistent and often comes with a refuse-to-file warning:


- **Hysingla ER (NDA 206627):** FDA set a limit of not more than 1.5 mcg/day for genotoxic impurities unless justified, required a Module 2 impurity table, and warned it might refuse to file if a structural-alert impurity above that level was not qualified[134](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=134)[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=135)[136](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=136) .
- **Tivorbex, Narcan, and Targiniq:** FDA gave similar warnings, tied to qualification above ICH thresholds and ICH M7 control strategies[137](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=137)[139](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=139)[140](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=140)[141](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=141)[142](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=142)[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=143) .
- **Kyprolis (NDA 202714):** At EOP2, FDA disagreed that genotoxicity had been fully assessed because the tested lots did not represent the impurity profile of other relevant lots[117](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=117) .
- **Viltepso (NDA 212154):** FDA said that if nonclinical impurity-qualification studies were needed, their final reports were expected in the original NDA, not afterward[132](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=132) .
- **Zurampic (NDA 207988):** FDA required an NDA table covering each structural-alert impurity's in silico results, toxicological assessment, and purge or control, at or below ICH M7 thresholds[119](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=119)[120](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=120) .


#### Container closure, extractables and leachables, and device constituents


E&L is the clearest example of pre-NDA advice that, when not followed, led to non-approval:


- **Cocaine hydrochloride nasal solution (Numbrino, NDA 209575):** The CRL stated that leachables had not been assessed on at least three to-be-marketed batches at multiple stability timepoints, "as advised" at the pre-NDA meeting. It required a new multibatch leachables study covering every marketed container closure system[420](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=420)[421](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=421) . The pre-NDA minutes for the same application (Numbrino) show that FDA had described those data as essential to setting shelf life[373](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=373)[374](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=374)[375](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=375) .
- **Brixadi (NDA 210136):** FDA had advised multibatch, multi-timepoint leachables testing. In review, it found the E&L evaluations inadequate, new data could not be reviewed in that cycle, and final reports were required with resubmission[385](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=385)[386](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=386) .
- **Anjeso (NDA 210583):** The original NDA received a CRL that cited an inadequate E&L evaluation: incompletely identified leachables, testing of one aged lot at one timepoint, and monitoring of only two compounds[387](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=387) .
- **Triferic (NDA 206317):** FDA said any leachable of concern found in an ongoing study had to be resolved before approval[371](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=371)[372](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=372) .


Device-constituent coordination can also affect timing. For Duopa (NDA 203952), FDA said cross-labeled devices submitted through 510(k) could not be cleared before NDA approval, so submission and clearance timing had to be coordinated[382](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=382) . For Nucala (BLA 761122), FDA told the applicant to include the actual E&L study reports in the BLA. FDA later requested them, and they were submitted during review[395](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=395) .


#### Facility inspection readiness


Pre-NDA and pre-BLA minutes almost always include standard advice: every manufacturing facility should be ready for GMP inspection at submission, and the application should list each site's FEI number, responsibilities, DMF reference, and onsite contact. Examples include Ryzodeg 70/30, Vimizim, Signifor LAR, Vyondys 53, and Sylvant[309](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=309)[277](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=277)[313](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=313)[314](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=314)[315](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=315) .


For Odomzo and Lonsurf, FDA also asked sponsors to identify non-commercial sites that made batches supporting the application[324](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=324) . For Firdapse, FDA noted that facility information could be submitted before the complete NDA. FDA could not request inspections before receiving the NDA but would work to make inspections timely afterward[311](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=311)[312](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=312) . For Emtriva, FDA asked the sponsor to state each site's inspection readiness. It also advised against delaying the CMC presubmission over unresolved starting-material questions, since those could be agreed during review[234](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=234) .


#### Insufficient CMC content in meeting packages


The quality of the briefing package affects how useful the meeting is. For Odomzo, FDA found no specific CMC information in the briefing materials and strongly recommended a CMC-only pre-NDA meeting before submission[225](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=225)[226](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=226) . For Ryaltris, FDA asked the sponsor to request a separate CMC pre-submission meeting[130](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=130) . For Mylotarg, a CMC-only Type C meeting led to requests for a separate 3.2.S module and BLA data on a newly identified attribute[462](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=462)[463](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=463) .

### Practical implications for CMC teams


1. **Treat EOP2 as the point to lock the commercial formulation and the dissolution method.** Changes after stability or Phase 3 start can trigger bridging studies or repeated clinical work[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=223)[32](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=32) .
2. **Plan stability backward from the submission date.** The default expectation is 12 months long-term and 6 months accelerated on three primary batches per strength[531](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=531)[535](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=535) . Any exception needs explicit, documented agreement with a defined update window[231](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=231)[527](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=527) .
3. **For biologics, complete PPQ and comparability before the BLA rather than relying on late submission**[453](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=453)[449](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=449)[467](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=467) .
4. **Close E&L and mutagenic impurity programs with multibatch, multi-timepoint data before filing.** This is where unaddressed pre-NDA advice has most visibly led to CRLs[420](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=420)[387](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=387) .
5. **Request a dedicated CMC meeting when the general milestone meeting cannot cover CMC adequately.** FDA has itself recommended this when packages were thin[191](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=191)[225](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/cmc-readiness-at-fda-end-of-phase-2-and-pre-ndapre?showSourceNumber=225) .
